indication: Advanced GIST after imatinib, in combination with sunitinib
headline: The FDA approved Ekitna (bezuclastinib) with sunitinib on November 24, 2026 for adults with advanced GIST previously treated with imatinib, on the PEAK trial, 6 days before its November 30 goal date.
pdufa_note: The FDA's notification states that on November 24, 2026 it approved bezuclastinib (Ekitna, Cogent Biosciences, Inc) in combination with sunitinib for adults with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors who have received prior treatment with imatinib (FDA, November 24, 2026). Cogent had disclosed a PDUFA goal date of November 30, 2026 for GIST (Cogent 8-K, August 10, 2026); the FDA acted 6 days early. The FDA's letter had not been posted on Drugs@FDA when this page was published. Per the FDA, in PEAK (NCT05208047), 413 patients, median progression-free survival was 16.5 months with bezuclastinib plus sunitinib and 9.2 months with sunitinib alone (hazard ratio 0.50, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.65); overall survival data were not mature. Cogent's systemic mastocytosis applications are separate and remain open.
h1: Ekitna (bezuclastinib) FDA approval for GIST, with sunitinib: Nov 24, 2026

indication: Adjuvant ER-positive, HER2-negative stage I to III breast cancer, intermediate to high risk
headline: The FDA approved Wilserdly (giredestrant) on November 23, 2026 as adjuvant treatment for ER-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer at intermediate to high risk of recurrence, on the lidERA trial, 7 days before its November 30 decision date.
pdufa_note: The FDA's notification states that on November 23, 2026 it approved giredestrant (Wilserdly, Genentech, Inc.) as a single agent for the adjuvant treatment of adults with ER-positive, HER2-negative, stage I, II and III breast cancer at intermediate to high risk of recurrence (FDA, November 23, 2026). Genentech announced it the same day (Genentech's announcement). Genentech had said the FDA was expected to decide by November 30, 2026 (Genentech, June 1, 2026); the FDA acted 7 days early. Per the FDA, in lidERA (NCT04961996), 4,170 patients, the 36-month invasive disease-free survival rate was 92.4% with giredestrant and 89.6% with standard endocrine therapy (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.57 to 0.87). The use with everolimus in ESR1-mutated advanced breast cancer was approved separately on November 16, 2026.
h1: Wilserdly (giredestrant) FDA approval for adjuvant early breast cancer: Nov 23, 2026

indication: Reduce surgical site infections in colorectal surgery with incisions longer than 20 cm
headline: PolyPid announced on November 24, 2026 that the FDA approved Bacfenssi (D-PLEX100) to reduce surgical site infections in colorectal surgery, on the Phase 3 SHIELD II trial.
pdufa_note: PolyPid announced on November 24, 2026 that the FDA approved its NDA for BACFENSSI (doxycycline hyclate), an extended-release paste previously known as D-PLEX100, to reduce the occurrence of surgical site infections in adults and pediatric patients weighing 45 kg or more undergoing colorectal surgery with incision lengths greater than 20 cm (PolyPid 6-K, Exhibit 99.1). PolyPid had disclosed a PDUFA target action date of November 28, 2026 under Priority Review (PolyPid 6-K, July 29, 2026), so the announcement came four days before it. The FDA's own record of the action day had not been read when this page was published, so no early or late margin is given yet. Per PolyPid, in SHIELD II the primary endpoint event occurred in 10.9% of patients on BACFENSSI plus standard of care and 18.1% on standard of care alone (p=0.004).
